column1: # cutgen-throttle-sweep configs: name<TAB>comma-separated overrides ("-" = none)
# Each override is KEY=VAL (env var, exported before mip-root-replay runs)
# or CLI:<arg> (extra mip-root-replay CLI argument).
# baseline: current shipped defaults -- GMI/LandP/RedSplit2 = root (per
# CbcSolver.cpp), filter extended to all three (CbcCutGenerator.cpp).
# As of 2026-09-24 the shipped per-round/per-lifetime cost-cap *values*
# were reverted to match this sweep's own "old-unthrottled" config below
# (CBC_REDSPLIT2_TIME_LIMIT=60, CBC_GMI_HOW_OFTEN=1, CBC_LANDP_TIME_LIMIT=1e30,
# etc -- see CbcSolverCutSetup.cpp) after this sweep showed old-unthrottled
# beating the originally-shipped tighter caps on both dual gap (30.66% vs
# 30.76%) and primal gap (12.85% vs 13.11%) at 128 nodes/2h, with no
# meaningful time cost. The independent RedSplit2 memory-safety fixes (row
# gate, dynamic maxNumComputedCuts*nrow buffer cap, and the
# mTab*card_contNonBasicVar tableau-size guard in CglRedSplit2.cpp) are
# unaffected by this and remain in effect regardless of these cap values.
baseline
# Disable each new generator individually, to isolate which one (if any)
# is driving a net win/loss over these first 128 nodes.
no-gmi
no-landp
no-redsplit2
# Disable all three -- the "these three generators shouldn't exist at all
# in this window" baseline the user asked to also check.
no-new-cuts
# Kept for reference: this is now numerically identical to "baseline"
# above (its values became the new shipped defaults on 2026-09-24). Left
# in the sweep so future re-runs still have an explicit, self-documenting
# override set that doesn't silently drift if the shipped defaults change
# again.
old-unthrottled
# Tighter throttles than the shipped defaults, to see if squeezing further
# still helps (or starts costing too much bound value). This sweep found
# it does not -- worst primal gap (13.58%) of all seven configs.
tighter-throttles
